LinkedIn has a reputation problem: r/LinkedInLunatics, viral takedown videos, and a whole genre of TikToks exist to mock its worst posts. Behind that layer, founders, operators, and consultants use LinkedIn to generate inbound deals, partnerships, and speaking invites without ads or cold outreach. 

This video covers the Authority Paradox, the Comment Flywheel, a bootstrapped CEO who built a $22M ARR company while posting tactical breakdowns, an MBE holder with brand deals at Google and Canva who's doubling down on personal branding, plus two Distinctiva client results that show what serious LinkedIn presence does for B2B businesses.

WHAT YOU'LL LEARN:
 Why LinkedIn Lunatics exists and which part of the criticism is fair
 The Authority Paradox: why the loudest mockers need LinkedIn the most
 What a $22M ARR founder on LinkedIn looks like
 Why someone with an MBE and blue chip clients still builds a personal brand
 Two real client outcomes: the VC operator, the billion dollar SaaS director
 How the Comment Flywheel multiplies reach beyond your follower count
 Why LinkedIn's ROI is invisible from the outside
 The early-platform window and why it's still open

KEY TAKEAWAYS:
 LinkedIn is the only platform where a single post reaches VPs, CMOs, and founders organically
 Visibility is a prerequisite for authority, credentials alone don't create inbound
 Reach on LinkedIn compounds through engagement networks, not follower count
 The DM three days after a post is where the ROI lives, and outsiders never see it
 Every platform's organic window closed after everyone caught on. LinkedIn's is still open
 The expensive mistake is letting the worst version of a platform decide whether you participate
